celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ قَوْلُ الْحَقِّ﴾ — with the nominative (rafʿ), as the khabar (predicate) of an implied (muqaddar) mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the word of the son of Maryam"; and with the accusative (naṣb) [قَوْلَ الْحَقِّ], with the implied verb "I say"; and the meaning is: the true word. ﴿الَّذِي فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ﴾ — from al-mirya (doubt), i.e. they doubt; and they are the Christians, who said that ʿĪsā is the son of Allah. They lied.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلَّهِ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ مِنْ وَلَدٍ سُبْحَانَهُ﴾ — declaring Him transcendent above that. ﴿إِذَا قَضَى أَمْرًا﴾ — i.e. wills to bring it into being, ﴿فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾ — with the nominative, with the implied "huwa" (it), and with the accusative, with the implied "an"; and among that is the creation of ʿĪsā without a father.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ﴾ — with fatḥa on "anna", with the implied "remember", and with kasra on it [وَإِنَّ], with the implied "say", as evidenced by {مَا قُلْتُ لَهُمْ إِلَّا مَا أَمَرْتَنِي بِهِ أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمْ}. ﴿هَذَا﴾ — what has been mentioned — ﴿صِرَاطٌ﴾ — a path — ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ — leading to Paradise.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿فَاخْتَلَفَ الْأَحْزَابُ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ﴾ — i.e. the Christians, concerning ʿĪsā: is he the son of Allah, or a god alongside Him, or the third of three? ﴿فَوَيْلٌ﴾ — so severity of punishment — ﴿لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ — by what has been mentioned and other than it — ﴿مِنْ مَشْهَدِ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ — i.e. the attendance of the Day of Resurrection and its terrors.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿أَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِرْ﴾ bihim — a form of exclamation (taʿajjub) meaning "how well they hear, and how well they see!" ﴿يَوْمَ يَأْتُونَنَا﴾ — in the Hereafter. ﴿لَكِنِ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ — this is putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun — ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ — i.e. in this world — ﴿فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ — i.e. clear; by it they have become deaf to hearing the truth and blind to seeing it. I.e.: marvel at them, O you addressed, at their hearing and their sight in the Hereafter, after they had been deaf and blind in this world.

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿وَأَنْذِرْهُمْ﴾ — warn, O Muḥammad, the disbelievers of Mecca — ﴿يَوْمَ الْحَسْرَةِ﴾ — it is the Day of Resurrection, in which the evildoer will feel regret over having abandoned doing good in this world — ﴿إِذْ قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ﴾ — for them in it, with punishment — ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ — in this world — ﴿فِي غَفْلَةٍ﴾ — about it — ﴿وَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — in it.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ﴾ — a tawkīd (emphasis) — ﴿نَرِثُ الْأَرْضَ وَمَنْ عَلَيْهَا﴾ — rational beings and others, by destroying them — ﴿وَإِلَيْنَا يُرْجَعُونَ﴾ — in it, for requital.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرْ﴾ — to them — ﴿فِي الْكِتَابِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ — i.e. his story. ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ صِدِّيقًا﴾ — exceedingly truthful — ﴿نَبِيًّا﴾ — and it is a badal (substitute) from his story.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ﴾ — Āzar — ﴿يَا أَبَتِ﴾ — the tāʾ is a replacement for the yāʾ of the possessive, and the two are not combined; and he used to worship idols — ﴿لِمَ تَعْبُدُ مَا لَا يَسْمَعُ وَلَا يُبْصِرُ وَلَا يُغْنِي عَنْكَ﴾ — does not suffice you — ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ — of benefit or harm?

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿يَا أَبَتِ إِنِّي قَدْ جَاءَنِي مِنَ الْعِلْمِ مَا لَمْ يَأْتِكَ فَاتَّبِعْنِي أَهْدِكَ صِرَاطًا﴾ — a path — ﴿سَوِيًّا﴾ — straight.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿يَا أَبَتِ لَا تَعْبُدِ الشَّيْطَانَ﴾ — by your obeying him in the worship of idols. ﴿إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَنِ عَصِيًّا﴾ — much given to disobedience.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿يَا أَبَتِ إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ يَمَسَّكَ عَذَابٌ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ — if you do not repent — ﴿فَتَكُونَ لِلشَّيْطَانِ وَلِيًّا﴾ — a helper and companion in the Fire.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿قَالَ أَرَاغِبٌ أَنْتَ عَنْ آلِهَتِي يَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ﴾ — so that you find fault with them? ﴿لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهِ﴾ — from attacking them — ﴿لَأَرْجُمَنَّكَ﴾ — with stones or with ugly words, so beware of me — ﴿وَاهْجُرْنِي مَلِيًّا﴾ — for a long time.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿قَالَ سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكَ﴾ — from me, i.e. I will not afflict you with anything hateful. ﴿سَأَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّي إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِي حَفِيًّا﴾ — from ḥafiya, i.e. gracious, so He answers my supplication. And he fulfilled his promise, mentioned in al-Shuʿarāʾ: {وَاغْفِرْ لِأَبِي}; and this was before it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, as He mentioned in Barāʾa.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَأَعْتَزِلُكُمْ وَمَا تَدْعُونَ﴾ — you worship — ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَأَدْعُوا﴾ — I worship — ﴿رَبِّي عَسَى﴾ — that — ﴿أَلَّا أَكُونَ بِدُعَاءِ رَبِّي﴾ — by worshipping Him — ﴿شَقِيًّا﴾ — as you have become wretched by worshipping idols.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا اعْتَزَلَهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ — by going to the Holy Land — ﴿وَهَبْنَا لَهُ﴾ — two sons, in whom he found comfort — ﴿إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَكُلًّا﴾ — of the two — ﴿جَعَلْنَا نَبِيًّا﴾.

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُمْ﴾ — to the three — ﴿مِنْ رَحْمَتِنَا﴾ — wealth and children — ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيًّا﴾ — exalted; it is the good praise among the people of all religions.

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ مُوسَى إِنَّهُ كَانَ مُخْلِصًا﴾ — with kasra on the lām, and with fatḥa on it [مُخْلَصًا]: from "he was sincere (akhlaṣa) in his worship" and "Allah purified him (khallaṣahu) from defilement" — ﴿وَكَانَ رَسُولًا نَبِيًّا﴾.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿وَنَادَيْنَاهُ﴾ — by saying "O Mūsā, indeed I am Allah" — ﴿مِنْ جَانِبِ الطُّورِ﴾ — the name of the mountain — ﴿الْأَيْمَنِ﴾ — i.e. the one on Mūsā's right as he came from Madyan — ﴿وَقَرَّبْنَاهُ نَجِيًّا﴾ — conversing intimately, in that Allah the Exalted made him hear His speech.

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ مِنْ رَحْمَتِنَا﴾ — Our grace — ﴿أَخَاهُ هَارُونَ﴾ — a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — ﴿نَبِيًّا﴾ — a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is what is intended by the gift, in answer to his request that He send his brother with him; and he was older than him.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ إِنَّهُ كَانَ صَادِقَ الْوَعْدِ﴾ — he never promised anything without fulfilling it; and he waited for someone he had promised for three days, or a year, until he returned to him at his place — ﴿وَكَانَ رَسُولًا﴾ — to Jurhum — ﴿نَبِيًّا﴾.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿وَكَانَ يَأْمُرُ أَهْلَهُ﴾ — i.e. his people — ﴿بِالصَّلَوةِ وَالزَّكَوةِ وَكَانَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ مَرْضِيًّا﴾ — its original form is marḍūwun; the two wāws were changed into two yāʾs and the ḍamma into a kasra.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ إِدْرِيسَ﴾ — he is the grandfather of Nūḥ's father — ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ صِدِّيقًا نَبِيًّا﴾.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا﴾ — he is alive in the fourth heaven, or the sixth, or the seventh, or in Paradise, which he was admitted into after he was made to taste death and was brought back to life, and he has not left it.

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ — a mubtadaʾ (subject) — ﴿الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ — an adjective (ṣifa) for it — ﴿مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ — an explication (bayān) of it, and it has the sense of an adjective; and what follows it up to the conditional clause is an adjective for "al-nabiyyīn". So His words ﴿مِنْ ذُرِّيَّةِ آدَمَ﴾ — i.e. Idrīs — ﴿وَمِمَّنْ حَمَلْنَا مَعَ نُوحٍ﴾ — in the ark, i.e. Ibrāhīm, the son of his son Sām — ﴿وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ — i.e. Ismāʿīl, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb — and of the offspring of ﴿وَإِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ — and he is Yaʿqūb, i.e. Mūsā, Hārūn, Zakariyyā, Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā — ﴿وَمِمَّنْ هَدَيْنَا وَاجْتَبَيْنَا﴾ — i.e. from among them. And the khabar (predicate) of "ulāʾika" is: ﴿إِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُ الرَّحْمَنِ خَرُّوا سُجَّدًا وَبُكِيًّا﴾ — plural of sājid (one prostrating) and bākin (one weeping); i.e. so be like them. The original form of bukiyy is bukuwy; the wāw was changed into a yāʾ and the ḍamma into a kasra.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿فَخَلَفَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ أَضَاعُوا الصَّلَوةَ﴾ — by abandoning it, like the Jews and the Christians — ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا الشَّهَوَاتِ﴾ — of acts of disobedience — ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَلْقَوْنَ غَيًّا﴾ — it is a valley in Hell, i.e. they will fall into it.

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ — but — ﴿مَنْ تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَأُولَئِكَ يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ — will not be diminished — ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ — of their reward.

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾ — of residence; a badal (substitute) from "al-janna" — ﴿الَّتِي وَعَدَ الرَّحْمَنُ عِبَادَهُ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ — a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. while absent from it. ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ وَعْدُهُ﴾ — i.e. what He has promised — ﴿مَأْتِيًّا﴾ — meaning "coming", and its original form is maʾtuwy; or what He has promised here is Paradise, which its people come to.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿لَا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْوًا﴾ — of speech — ﴿إِلَّا﴾ — but they hear — ﴿سَلَامًا﴾ — from the angels upon them, or from one another — ﴿وَلَهُمْ رِزْقُهُمْ فِيهَا بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا﴾ — i.e. according to the measure of these two in this world; and in Paradise there is neither day nor night, but light and radiance forever.

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿تِلْكَ الْجَنَّةُ الَّتِي نُورِثُ﴾ — We give and bestow — ﴿مِنْ عِبَادِنَا مَنْ كَانَ تَقِيًّا﴾ — through his obedience. And the following was revealed when revelation was delayed for some days and the Prophet ﷺ said to Jibrīl, "What prevents you from visiting us?":

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿وَمَا نَتَنَزَّلُ إِلَّا بِأَمْرِ رَبِّكَ لَهُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِينَا﴾ — i.e. before us, of the affairs of the Hereafter — ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَنَا﴾ — of the affairs of this world — ﴿وَمَا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ﴾ — i.e. whatever happens from this time until the Hour is established; i.e. to Him belongs the knowledge of all of that. ﴿وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ نَسِيًّا﴾ — meaning "forgetful", i.e. abandoning you by delaying revelation from you.

celaleyn:65-65.t: He is ﴿رَبُّ﴾ — the Owner of — ﴿السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فَاعْبُدْهُ وَاصْطَبِرْ لِعِبَادَتِهِ﴾ — i.e. be patient in it. ﴿هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُ سَمِيًّا﴾ — i.e. one named with that? No.

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُ الْإِنْسَانُ﴾ — who denies the resurrection, Ubayy ibn Khalaf or al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, concerning whom the verse was revealed — ﴿أَإِذَا﴾ — with the second hamza pronounced fully (taḥqīq) or lightened (tashīl), and with the alif inserted between the two in both of its ways, and between the other [Translator's note: the phrase «وَبَيْنَ الْأُخْرَى» is elliptical as written] — ﴿مَا مِتُّ لَسَوْفَ أُخْرَجُ حَيًّا﴾ — from the grave, as Muḥammad says? So the interrogative has the meaning of negation, i.e. I will not be brought to life after death. And "mā" is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and likewise the lām. And he was answered by His words, the Exalted:

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿أَوَلَا يَذَّكَّرُ الْإِنْسَانُ أَنَّا﴾ — its original form is yatadhakkaru; the tāʾ was changed into a dhāl and assimilated into the dhāl; and in one reading it is dropped, with sukūn on the dhāl and ḍamma on the kāf [يَذْكُرُ] — ﴿خَلَقْنَاهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَمْ يَكُ شَيْئًا﴾ — so that he may infer the restoration from the first creation.

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿فَوَرَبِّكَ لَنَحْشُرَنَّهُمْ﴾ — i.e. those who deny the resurrection — ﴿وَالشَّيَاطِينَ﴾ — i.e. We will gather each of them with his devil in a chain — ﴿ثُمَّ لَنُحْضِرَنَّهُمْ حَوْلَ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ — from outside it — ﴿جِثِيًّا﴾ — on their knees; plural of jāthin, and its original form is juthuwwun or juthuwiyyun, from jathā yajthū or yajthī — two dialects.

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿ثُمَّ لَنَنْزِعَنَّ مِنْ كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ﴾ — party among them — ﴿أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ عَلَى الرَّحْمَنِ عِتِيًّا﴾ — in audacity.

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿ثُمَّ لَنَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِالَّذِينَ هُمْ أَوْلَى بِهَا﴾ — more deserving of Hell, the most severe and others among them — ﴿صِلِيًّا﴾ — entering and burning, so We will begin with them; its original form is ṣuluwiyy, from ṣaliya, with kasra on the lām and with fatḥa on it.

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ — i.e. "not" — ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ — anyone — ﴿إِلَّا وَارِدُهَا﴾ — i.e. entering Hell. ﴿كَانَ عَلَى رَبِّكَ حَتْمًا مَقْضِيًّا﴾ — He has made it binding and decreed it; He will not leave it.

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي﴾ — with shadda and without — ﴿الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾ — idolatry (shirk) and disbelief — from it, ﴿وَنَذَرُ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ — through idolatry and disbelief — ﴿فِيهَا جِثِيًّا﴾ — on their knees.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿وَإِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ — i.e. the believers and the disbelievers — ﴿آيَاتُنَا﴾ — of the Quran — ﴿بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ — clear; a ḥāl (circumstantial) — ﴿قَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَيُّ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ﴾ — we or you — ﴿خَيْرٌ مَقَامًا﴾ — in residence and dwelling; with fatḥa from qāma, and with ḍamma from aqāma — ﴿وَأَحْسَنُ نَدِيًّا﴾ — meaning al-nādī, which is the gathering place of a people where they converse. They mean: we, so we are better than you. The Exalted said:

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿وَكَمْ﴾ — i.e. many — ﴿أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ﴾ — i.e. a nation of the past nations — ﴿هُمْ أَحْسَنُ أَثَاثًا﴾ — in wealth and goods — ﴿وَرِئْيًا﴾ — in appearance, from al-ruʾya (seeing). So just as We destroyed them for their disbelief, We will destroy these.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿قُلْ مَنْ كَانَ فِي الضَّلَالَةِ﴾ — a condition (sharṭ), whose apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is ﴿فَلْيَمْدُدْ﴾ — with the meaning of a statement, i.e. He extends — ﴿لَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ مَدًّا﴾ — in this world, leading him on step by step — ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا رَأَوْا مَا يُوعَدُونَ إِمَّا الْعَذَابَ﴾ — such as killing and capture — ﴿وَإِمَّا السَّاعَةَ﴾ — which includes Hell, so they will enter it — ﴿فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ هُوَ شَرٌّ مَكَانًا وَأَضْعَفُ جُنْدًا﴾ — in helpers: they or the believers. Their troops are the devils, and the troops of the believers are the angels.

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿وَيَزِيدُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا﴾ — through faith — ﴿هُدًى﴾ — through the verses sent down upon them. ﴿وَالْبَاقِيَاتُ الصَّالِحَاتُ﴾ — it is obedience, which remains for the one who does it — ﴿خَيْرٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَابًا وَخَيْرٌ مَرَدًّا﴾ — i.e. what is returned and comes back to him, unlike the deeds of the disbelievers. The "betterness" here is set against their saying "which of the two parties is better in station?"

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ — al-ʿĀṣī ibn Wāʾil — ﴿وَقَالَ﴾ — to Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt, who had said to him "You will be resurrected after death" and who was demanding money from him — ﴿لَأُوتَيَنَّ﴾ — on the supposition of the resurrection — ﴿مَالًا وَوَلَدًا﴾ — and then I will pay you back.

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿أَطَّلَعَ الْغَيْبَ﴾ — i.e. does he know it, and that he will be given what he said? The interrogative hamza made the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) unnecessary, so it was dropped. ﴿أَمِ اتَّخَذَ عِنْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ عَهْدًا﴾ — that he will be given what he said?

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ — i.e. he will not be given that. ﴿سَنَكْتُبُ﴾ — We will order the writing of — ﴿مَا يَقُولُ وَنَمُدُّ لَهُ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ مَدًّا﴾ — We will increase him thereby in punishment above the punishment of his disbelief.

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿وَنَرِثُهُ مَا يَقُولُ﴾ — of wealth and children — ﴿وَيَأْتِينَا﴾ — on the Day of Resurrection — ﴿فَرْدًا﴾ — having neither wealth nor children.

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿وَاتَّخَذُوا﴾ — i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca — ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ — the idols — ﴿آلِهَةً﴾ — whom they worship — ﴿لِيَكُونُوا لَهُمْ عِزًّا﴾ — intercessors with Allah, so that they would not be punished.

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ — i.e. there is nothing to prevent their punishment. ﴿سَيَكْفُرُونَ﴾ — i.e. the gods — ﴿بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ﴾ — i.e. they will deny it, as in another verse: {مَا كَانُوا إِيَّانَا يَعْبُدُونَ} — ﴿وَيَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدًّا﴾ — helpers and enemies.

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا الشَّيَاطِينَ﴾ — We have given them power — ﴿عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ تَؤُزُّهُمْ﴾ — inciting them to acts of disobedience — ﴿أَزًّا﴾.

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿فَلَا تَعْجَلْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ — by seeking the punishment. ﴿إِنَّمَا نَعُدُّ لَهُمْ﴾ — the days and nights, or the breaths — ﴿عَدًّا﴾ — until the time of their punishment. Remember:

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿يَوْمَ نَحْشُرُ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ — through their faith — ﴿إِلَى الرَّحْمَنِ وَفْدًا﴾ — plural of wāfid, meaning a rider.

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿وَنَسُوقُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ — through their disbelief — ﴿إِلَى جَهَنَّمَ وِرْدًا﴾ — plural of wārid, meaning one walking, thirsty.

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿لَا يَمْلِكُونَ﴾ — i.e. people — ﴿الشَّفَاعَةَ إِلَّا مَنِ اتَّخَذَ عِنْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ عَهْدًا﴾ — i.e. the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and there is no power and no strength except through Allah.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ — i.e. the Jews and the Christians and whoever claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah — ﴿اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَنُ وَلَدًا﴾. The Exalted said to them:

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئًا إِدًّا﴾ — i.e. a monstrous, abhorrent thing.

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿تَكَادُ﴾ — with tāʾ and with yāʾ — ﴿السَّمَاوَاتُ يَنْفَطِرْنَ﴾ — with nūn, and in one reading with tāʾ and shadda on the ṭāʾ [يَتَفَطَّرْنَ] — by splitting apart ﴿مِنْهُ وَتَنْشَقُّ الْأَرْضُ وَتَخِرُّ الْجِبَالُ هَدًّا﴾ — i.e. close in upon them because of

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿أَنْ دَعَوْا لِلرَّحْمَنِ وَلَدًا﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here; the ayah completes the sentence begun in the gloss on the previous ayah ("because of").]

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿وَمَا يَنْبَغِي لِلرَّحْمَنِ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًا﴾ — i.e. that is not befitting for Him.

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ — i.e. "not" — ﴿كُلُّ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِلَّا آتِي الرَّحْمَنِ عَبْدًا﴾ — abased and submissive on the Day of Resurrection; among them are ʿUzayr and ʿĪsā.

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿لَقَدْ أَحْصَاهُمْ وَعَدَّهُمْ عَدًّا﴾ — so neither the total of all of them nor a single one of them is hidden from Him.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿وَكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ فَرْدًا﴾ — without wealth and without a helper to protect him.

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ سَيَجْعَلُ لَهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ وُدًّا﴾ — among themselves: they show affection and love one another, and Allah the Exalted loves them.

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَاهُ﴾ — i.e. the Quran — ﴿بِلِسَانِكَ﴾ — the Arabic — ﴿لِتُبَشِّرَ بِهِ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ — those who attain success through faith — ﴿وَتُنْذِرَ﴾ — warn — ﴿بِهِ قَوْمًا لُدًّا﴾ — plural of aladd, i.e. one who disputes with falsehood; and they are the disbelievers of Mecca.

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿وَكَمْ﴾ — i.e. many — ﴿أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ﴾ — i.e. a nation of the past nations, for their denying the messengers. ﴿هَلْ تُحِسُّ﴾ — do you find — ﴿مِنْهُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ أَوْ تَسْمَعُ لَهُمْ رِكْزًا﴾ — a faint sound? No. So just as We destroyed those, We will destroy these.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿كهيعص﴾ Allah knows best what He means by that. This [is]: [Translator's note: the sentence continues into the next entry, 19:2.]

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿ذِكْرُ رَحْمَتِ رَبِّكَ عَبْدَهُ﴾ the object of رَحْمَة ﴿زَكَرِيَّا﴾ an explication (bayān) of it.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿إِذْ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) رَحْمَة ﴿نَادَى رَبَّهُ نِدَاءً﴾ containing a supplication ﴿خَفِيًّا﴾ secretly, in the depth of the night, because that is quicker to be answered.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَهَنَ﴾ has weakened ﴿الْعَظْمُ﴾ all of it ﴿مِنِّي وَاشْتَعَلَ الرَّأْسُ﴾ of me ﴿شَيْبًا﴾ a tamyīz (specification) converted from the fāʿil (agent), i.e. grey hair has spread in his hair as fire spreads in firewood; and I wish to call upon You ﴿وَلَمْ أَكُنْ بِدُعَائِكَ﴾ i.e. in my calling upon You ﴿رَبِّ شَقِيًّا﴾ i.e. disappointed in the past, so do not disappoint me in what is to come.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَإِنِّي خِفْتُ الْمَوَالِيَ﴾ i.e. those who come after me in lineage, such as the paternal cousins ﴿مِنْ وَرَائِي﴾ i.e. after my death, [fearing] for the religion, that they would neglect it, as I have witnessed among the Children of Israel in the alteration of the religion ﴿وَكَانَتِ امْرَأَتِي عَاقِرًا﴾ not bearing children ﴿فَهَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ﴾ from You ﴿وَلِيًّا﴾ a son

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يَرِثْنِي﴾ in the jussive, as the answer to the imperative, and in the nominative [يَرِثُنِي] as an adjective (ṣifa) of وَلِيًّا ﴿وَيَرِثُ﴾ in both ways ﴿مِنْ آلِ يَعْقُوبَ﴾ my ancestor, knowledge and prophethood ﴿وَاجْعَلْهُ رَبِّ رَضِيًّا﴾ i.e. pleasing to You. Allah the Exalted said, answering his request for the son through whom His mercy came about:

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿يَا زَكَرِيَّا إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَامٍ﴾ who will inherit, as you asked ﴿اسْمُهُ يَحْيَى لَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا﴾ i.e. anyone named Yaḥyā.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّى﴾ how ﴿يَكُونُ لِي غُلَامٌ وَكَانَتِ امْرَأَتِي عَاقِرًا وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ الْكِبَرِ عِتِيًّا﴾ from عَتَا, "became dry", i.e. to the limit of age, one hundred and twenty years, while his wife had reached ninety-eight years. The origin of عِتِيّ is عُتُوّ; the tāʾ was given kasra for lightness, the first wāw was changed to yāʾ to suit the kasra, and the second to yāʾ so that the [first] yāʾ could be assimilated into it.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ the matter is ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ namely creating a boy from the two of you ﴿قَالَ رَبُّكَ هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ﴾ i.e. that I restore to you the power of intercourse and open your wife's womb for conception ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَمْ تَكُ شَيْئًا﴾ before your creation. And so that Allah might display this great power, He inspired him to ask, so that he would be answered with what indicates it. And when his soul longed for the swift coming of what he had been given glad tidings of,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ لِي آيَةً﴾ i.e. a sign of my wife's pregnancy ﴿قَالَ آيَتُكَ﴾ of it ﴿أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ النَّاسَ﴾ i.e. you will be withheld from speaking to them, unlike the remembrance of Allah ﴿ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ﴾ i.e. with their days ﴿سَوِيًّا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of تُكَلِّمُ, i.e. without any illness.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿فَخَرَجَ عَلَى قَوْمِهِ مِنَ الْمِحْرَابِ﴾ i.e. the place of prayer; they were waiting for him to open it so that they could pray in it at his command, as was customary ﴿فَأَوْحَى﴾ he signalled ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ أَنْ سَبِّحُوا﴾ pray ﴿بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا﴾ at the beginning and end of the day, as customary. So by his being prevented from speaking to them he knew of her pregnancy with Yaḥyā. And two years after his birth Allah the Exalted said to him:

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿يَا يَحْيَى خُذِ الْكِتَابَ﴾ i.e. the Torah ﴿بِقُوَّةٍ﴾ with earnestness ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ الْحُكْمَ﴾ prophethood ﴿صَبِيًّا﴾ at three years of age.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَحَنَانًا﴾ mercy for people ﴿مِنْ لَدُنَّا﴾ from Us ﴿وَزَكَوةً﴾ charity towards them ﴿وَكَانَ تَقِيًّا﴾ It is narrated that he never committed a sin nor intended one.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَبَرًّا بِوَالِدَيْهِ﴾ i.e. doing good to them ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُنْ جَبَّارًا﴾ arrogant ﴿عَصِيًّا﴾ disobedient to his Lord.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَسَلَامٌ﴾ from Us ﴿عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوْمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَيًّا﴾ i.e. on these fearful days, in which one sees what one has not seen before, he is safe.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Quran ﴿مَرْيَمَ﴾ i.e. her story ﴿إِذْ﴾ when ﴿انْتَبَذَتْ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا مَكَانًا شَرْقِيًّا﴾ i.e. she withdrew to a place towards the east of the house.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿فَاتَّخَذَتْ مِنْ دُونِهِمْ حِجَابًا﴾ she let down a curtain to screen herself, in order to comb her hair or clean her clothes, or to bathe from her menstruation ﴿فَأَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهَا رُوحَنَا﴾ Gabriel ﴿فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهَا﴾ after she had put on her clothes ﴿بَشَرًا سَوِيًّا﴾ perfect in form.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿قَالَتْ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِالرَّحْمَنِ مِنْكَ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَقِيًّا﴾ so desist from me because of my seeking refuge.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّمَا أَنَا رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِأَهَبَ لَكِ غُلَامًا زَكِيًّا﴾ with prophethood.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿قَالَتْ أَنَّى يَكُونُ لِي غُلَامٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِي بَشَرٌ﴾ through marriage ﴿وَلَمْ أَكُ بَغِيًّا﴾ an adulteress.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ the matter is ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ namely creating a boy from you without a father ﴿قَالَ رَبُّكِ هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ﴾ i.e. that Gabriel breathe into you by My command, so that you conceive him; and because what has been mentioned has the meaning of a reason, [the following] is conjoined to it: ﴿وَلِنَجْعَلَهُ آيَةً لِلنَّاسِ﴾ of Our power ﴿وَرَحْمَةً مِنَّا﴾ for whoever believes in him ﴿وَكَانَ﴾ his creation ﴿أَمْرًا مَقْضِيًّا﴾ decreed in My knowledge. So Gabriel breathed into the opening of her shift, and she felt the pregnancy in her womb, already formed.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿فَحَمَلَتْهُ فَانْتَبَذَتْ﴾ withdrew ﴿بِهِ مَكَانًا قَصِيًّا﴾ far from her family.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿فَأَجَاءَهَا﴾ brought her ﴿الْمَخَاضُ﴾ the pains of childbirth ﴿إِلَى جِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾ to lean on it; so she gave birth; and the conception, the forming and the birth were in one hour ﴿قَالَتْ يَا﴾ for calling attention ﴿لَيْتَنِي مِتُّ قَبْلَ هَذَا﴾ matter ﴿وَكُنْتُ نَسْيًا مَنْسِيًّا﴾ a thing abandoned, neither known nor mentioned.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ i.e. Gabriel, who was below her ﴿أَلَّا تَحْزَنِي قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾ a stream of water which had dried up.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾ it was dry, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) ﴿تُسَاقِطْ﴾ originally with two tāʾs; the second was changed into sīn and assimilated into the sīn; in one reading it is dropped [تُسَاقِطُ] ﴿عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا﴾ tamyīz (specification) ﴿جَنِيًّا﴾ its adjective (ṣifa).

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿فَكُلِي﴾ of the fresh dates ﴿وَاشْرَبِي﴾ from the stream ﴿وَقَرِّي عَيْنًا﴾ with the child; a tamyīz (specification) converted from the fāʿil (agent), i.e. let your eye be cooled by him, i.e. be at rest and not long for anything else ﴿فَإِمَّا﴾ in it the nūn of the conditional إِنْ is assimilated into the redundant مَا ﴿تَرَيِنَّ﴾ from it the lām and the ʿayn of the verb were dropped, the vowel [of the ʿayn] was transferred to the rāʾ, and the yāʾ of the pronoun was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters ﴿مِنَ الْبَشَرِ أَحَدًا﴾ who asks you about your child ﴿فَقُولِي إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ صَوْمًا﴾ i.e. abstaining from speech about him and about other matters with people, as evidenced by ﴿فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ الْيَوْمَ إِنْسِيًّا﴾ i.e. after that.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿فَأَتَتْ بِهِ قَوْمَهَا تَحْمِلُهُ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial); and they saw him ﴿قَالُوا يَا مَرْيَمُ لَقَدْ جِئْتِ شَيْئًا فَرِيًّا﴾ grave, in that you have brought a child without a father.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿يَا أُخْتَ هَارُونَ﴾ he was a righteous man, i.e. O you who resemble him in chastity ﴿مَا كَانَ أَبُوكِ امْرَأَ سَوْءٍ﴾ i.e. a fornicator ﴿وَمَا كَانَتْ أُمُّكِ بَغِيًّا﴾ i.e. an adulteress; so where did you get this child from?

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿فَأَشَارَتْ﴾ to them ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ that they should speak to him ﴿قَالُوا كَيْفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَنْ كَانَ﴾ i.e. is ﴿فِي الْمَهْدِ صَبِيًّا﴾

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿قَالَ إِنِّي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ آتَانِيَ الْكِتَابَ﴾ i.e. the Gospel ﴿وَجَعَلَنِي نَبِيًّا﴾

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿وَجَعَلَنِي مُبَارَكًا أَيْنَ مَا كُنْتُ﴾ i.e. of much benefit to people; a report of what was written [decreed] for him ﴿وَأَوْصَانِي بِالصَّلَوةِ وَالزَّكَوةِ﴾ He commanded me with them ﴿مَا دُمْتُ حَيًّا﴾

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَبَرًّا بِوَالِدَتِي﴾ accusative by an implied جَعَلَنِي ﴿وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْنِي جَبَّارًا﴾ self-aggrandising ﴿شَقِيًّا﴾ disobedient to his Lord.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَالسَّلَامُ﴾ from Allah ﴿عَلَيَّ يَوْمَ وُلِدْتُ وَيَوْمَ أَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ أُبْعَثُ حَيًّا﴾ What was said earlier about the master Yaḥyā is said about this.
